title: Building a Line Between Two Points
description: A point is a position. A line is a relation. Watch how two endpoints create distance, direction, and the first hint that whole numbers resist.

capture_leaks.curvature: wavefunctions — a line is always straight; waves bend it into sine and cosine
capture_leaks.thickness: later primitives — a line has no width; cylinders, tubes, meshes add extent
capture_leaks.meaning: graphtheory — a line connects two points but says nothing about what they share; edges carry semantics
capture_leaks.multiplicity: Point_Lines — one line tells you about a relation; many lines tell you about a system
capture_leaks.discreteness_at_integer: randomness, foundationscrisis — the integer glitch teaches that whole numbers are an imposition, not a property of space

limit: This line is straight, thin, alone, and meaningless. Each silence is a question. A curved line is a wave. A thick line is a mesh. A line among lines is a network. The line you built is the atom of all these structures.

stages.title: Two points make a relation
stages.thinking: In Point_One you held a single point. Now there are two. The moment you have two positions, you have something new — the space between them. Distance. Direction. A line is not a thing. It is a relation between two things.

stages.title: Make the relation visible
stages.thinking: Distance is a number. Direction is a vector. Neither is visible. We create a CylinderMesh stretched between the two points — the same technique from interactive_point_origin’s line to origin. Position at midpoint, height equals distance, orient toward the endpoint.

stages.title: Orient the cylinder
stages.thinking: A cylinder stands upright by default. To make it point from A to B, we need to build a rotation basis from the direction vector. This is the first real transform — creating an orthonormal basis from a direction. Three perpendicular vectors that define how the cylinder faces.
stages.code:
func update_line_transform(start_pos: Vector3, end_pos: Vector3):
	var cylinder = current_line.mesh as CylinderMesh
	var distance = start_pos.distance_to(end_pos)
	cylinder.height = distance
	
	var center_pos = (start_pos + end_pos) / 2.0
	current_line.position = center_pos
	
	# Build orientation from direction
	var direction = (end_pos - start_pos).normalized()
	var up = Vector3.UP
	var right = direction.cross(up).normalized()
	if right.length() < 0.001:  # direction is parallel to UP
		right = Vector3.RIGHT
		up = right.cross(direction).normalized()
	else:
		up = right.cross(direction).normalized()
	
	# Apply the basis
	current_line.transform.basis = Basis(right, direction, up)

stages.title: Show the measurement
stages.thinking: The line has length. The label makes it readable — a billboard Label3D floating above the midpoint, updating every frame. The number is formatted to two decimal places. This is the bridge between felt distance and named distance.
stages.code:
func create_length_label():
	length_label = Label3D.new()
	length_label.billboard = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
	length_label.font_size = 32
	length_label.modulate = Color(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.8)
	length_label.outline_size = 4
	length_label.scale = Vector3.ONE * 0.1
	add_child(length_label)

func update_length_label(start_pos: Vector3, end_pos: Vector3):
	var distance = start_pos.distance_to(end_pos)
	length_label.text = "Length: %.2fm" % distance
	
	# Position at midpoint, slightly above
	var center_pos = (start_pos + end_pos) / 2.0
	center_pos.y += 0.05
	length_label.position = center_pos

stages.title: Update every frame
stages.thinking: Both endpoints are grabbable. The player moves them freely. So the line must update every frame — recalculate height, reposition at midpoint, reorient, relabel. This is the _process loop: the heartbeat that keeps the relation alive as its constituents change.

stages.title: Whole numbers resist
stages.thinking: This is the critical interaction. When the distance approaches an integer — 0.97m, 1.03m — the line fights back. It jitters. It crackles. The controller vibrates. The label flashes red. Why? Because whole numbers are a human imposition. Nature doesn’t prefer 1.0 over 0.97. The glitch makes you feel that discreteness is a choice, not a given.

stages.title: Synthesize the glitch sound
stages.thinking: The crackle is not a file. It’s generated from white noise with random spikes — the same synthesis technique from interactive_point_origin’s pickup tone, but harsher. A looping AudioStreamWAV that plays silently until resistance activates, then fades in. The sound of a number asserting itself.

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The line knows what it is. It is not an object — it is defined entirely by its two endpoints. The resistance at integer lengths is not a bug. It is the pedagogical core: the privilege of whole numbers, felt through the body before named by the mind.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: length = |p2 - p1| — the distance between two points, made visible and tangible
# desire: learner feels a line as relationship, not object — it exists because two points exist
# critical_parameter: the glitch/haptic resistance when length is near an integer
# triggers: dragging either end grab sphere — length label updates live, glitch fires at integer thresholds
# emerges: the privilege of whole numbers; the line as a tension between two positions
# needs: Label3D [has], both endpoints are grabbable [has]
# relationships: depends on two static_points; unlocks all polygon primitives
# truth: a line segment has no intrinsic existence — it is defined entirely by its two endpoints
